_description: Type-spelling synonyms: a node `type` that is not a section of attribute_definitions.json, mapped to the section that declares it (`canonical`).

The one table. Validation (jui_cli alias_table.py, the Ruby attribute_validator_core.rb) and the renderers read it: the sjui SwiftUI, kjui Compose and rjui React converters (shared/core/type_synonyms.rb), and SwiftJsonUI and KotlinJsonUI Dynamic (each through a vendored copy). None holds a list of its own. Not a reader: sjui's UIKit mode, a separate renderer with its own set of UIKit components and its own spellings for them (Table is its SJUITableView); it draws what it has, and this table does not apply to it.

A renderer draws a synonym as its canonical type — except where the entry names `render_as`: the spelling draws differently from its canonical type (CircleImage clips to a circle), and the renderer draws `render_as` with the converter of that name, while validation still reads the canonical section. A type an app registers as its own component is the app's, whatever its spelling, and is never rewritten.

Any other key of an entry is an attribute the spelling itself means, of the canonical section: HStack and Row are a View with `orientation: horizontal`, VStack and Column one with `vertical`. A renderer adds it when the node does not set it. When the node sets it otherwise (an HStack with `orientation: vertical`), the node's value is drawn and the renderer warns, naming both. ZStack and Box add nothing: a View without orientation is already the stack they mean.

Not here: EditText / Input / Check / Toggle. They are sections of attribute_definitions.json that point at their canonical section with `_alias_of`; the exact-match lookup finds them first. Spacer / Divider / Triangle are neither declared nor synonyms, and draw as undeclared types.
